To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the intensity of a carotenoid-based secondary sexual signal was significantly reduced in a population of birds that had been exposed to high levels of radiation from Chernobyl, and that the intensity of this signal was positively related to immune function in the control populations, but negatively related to it in the exposed population.

(1) the intensity of carotenoids–based sexual colorations was significantly lower in the population of barn swallows exposed to radioactive contamination compared to the two control populations; (2) the positive covariations between the intensity of carotene–based coloration and the size of a sexually selected trait (the length of outer tail feathers) disappeared in the population of swallows exposed to high levels of radioactive contamination; (3) lymphocyte and immunoglobulins concentrations were depressed,
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of exposure to radioactive contamination on sexual signals, immune function, and the relationship between the two.
the role of carotenoids in sexual signalling and immune function.
the relationship between the intensity of carotenoids–based sexual signals and the immune system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in the population of barn swallows living near Chernobyl, the use of carotenoid-based coloration for sexual signalling has been traded against its use for immune function.
the immune system of the birds is affected by radiation, which in turn leads to a decrease in the intensity of carotenoids in the plumage.
carotenoid–dependent sexual coloration is not reliable under conditions of intense environmental stress.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the intensity of carotenoids in the plumage of barn swallows is related to their concentration in the blood and that this is in turn related to the level of immune function in the Chernobil population.
the intensity of carotenoids–based sexual colorations was lower in birds from Chernobyl, compared to the control populations.
the intensity of carotenoids in sexual signals is related to the intensity of the immune function, and the intensity of both is related to the exposure to radioactive contamination.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Chernobyl accident provides an opportunity to study how the immune system and the expression of sexual signals are affected by exposure to high levels of radiation.
environmental stressors can have profound effects on the immune systems of wild animals.
environmental stress can disrupt the relationship between carotenoid-based coloration and immune function.
